rows.message: How does receivables advance (antecipação) work with Getnet?
rows.answer:
Here is how receivables advance (antecipação) works with Getnet:

- **What it does:** You receive money from credit sales early. This covers both single-payment and installment sales. You don't have to wait for the normal settlement period. [sup-duvidas-12]
- **When you can advance:** A schedule can be advanced from D+1 (one business day after the sale) up to D-3 (three business days before it settles). [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10]
- **Authorization:** Under the new rules, you must authorize Getnet to query your schedule at the Registradora. The Registradora confirms the authorization and the operation. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09]
- **Costs:** There are no extra charges beyond the existing ones: rental, MDR and the antecipação fee. The sources I found don't give the fee amount. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09]
- **Limitation:** Sales from some card brands can't be advanced through Getnet. For those, you have to go directly to the card issuer or operator. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10]

rows.message: How does receivables advance (antecipação) work with Getnet?
rows.answer:
Getnet's sales advance (antecipação de vendas) lets you receive credit sale amounts early. This covers both single-payment and installment sales. You don't have to wait for the normal settlement period [sup-duvidas-12].

- **Timing:** You can advance a sale from D+1 (one business day after the sale). You can do it up to D-3 (three business days before the scheduled settlement) [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10].
- **Authorization:** Under the new rules, you must consent to Getnet querying your schedule at the Registradora. The Registradora confirms the authorization and the operation [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09].
- **Costs:** There are no charges beyond the existing ones. Those are rental, MDR and the advance fee (taxa de antecipação) [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09].
- **Card brands:** Some brands can't be advanced through Getnet. For those, you have to go directly to the card issuer or operator [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10].

The sources don't say which brands are affected or what the advance fee is.

rows.message: How does receivables advance (antecipação) work with Getnet?
rows.answer:
Receivables advance (antecipação de vendas) lets you receive credit sale amounts early. This covers sales paid in full or in installments. You don't have to wait for the normal settlement period. [sup-duvidas-12]

- **Timing:** You can advance a schedule from D+1 (one business day after the sale) up to D-3 (three business days before it settles). [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10]
- **Authorization:** Under the new rules, you must authorize Getnet to query your schedule at the Registradora (registry). This confirms your consent and the operation. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09]
- **Costs:** There are no extra charges beyond the existing ones, such as rental, MDR and the advance fee. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-09]
- **Limitation:** Sales from some card brands can't be advanced through Getnet. For those, you have to go to the card issuer/operator. [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10]

The sources don't say which brands are affected or what the advance fee is.
